title: FACTR: Force-Attending Curriculum Training for Contact-Rich Policy Learning
abstract: Many contact-rich tasks humans perform rely on force feedback, but this information, readily available in most robot arms, is not commonly used in teleoperation and policy learning. FACTR presents (1) a low-cost bilateral teleoperation setup that relays external follower-arm forces back to the teacher arm, and (2) a policy learning method employing a curriculum that corrupts visual input with decreasing intensity throughout training. The curriculum prevents a transformer policy from over-fitting to vision and guides it to attend to the force modality, improving generalization to unseen objects by ~40% over a no-curriculum force baseline.
